summary: Defines the terminology used when discussing SPEERMINT, which concerns how voice and multimedia providers connect with each other over IP. It is a shared vocabulary so that related documents use words consistently.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5486 defines terms used to describe providers exchanging SIP session traffic. It distinguishes session-layer peering from IP routing peering and explains the functions and agreements involved.

questions: what is a federation in speermint
subtitle: Shared terminology for SIP-based session peering between multimedia service providers.

tldr.problem: Providers used the word peering for different kinds of interconnection, making discussions of SIP call routing unclear.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines terms for session-layer peering, its direct and indirect forms, associated functions, and federations of providers.
tldr.outcome: The document establishes vocabulary for SPEERMINT work. In this memo, peering refers to interconnection between SIP service providers at the session layer.

today: RFC 5486 is Informational and was published in March 2009. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What SPEERMINT Covers
sections.content:
Voice over IP peering has referred to several ways that service-provider networks connect and deliver SIP calls. RFC 5486 focuses on session-layer interconnection between SIP servers, rather than interconnection for exchanging IP routing information.

The framework uses existing protocols such as SIP and ENUM as building blocks. It defines vocabulary for real-time and quasi-real-time sessions, including non-voice communication that uses SIP signaling.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC defines words for describing SIP-based session interconnection. It separates that topic from IP-layer routing between providers.

sections.title: Border Elements and Session Data
sections.content:
A Signaling Path Border Element (SBE) handles session-layer messages at a domain boundary. It may translate between signaling protocols, hide identity or topology, or enforce admission control. A Data Path Border Element (DBE) handles media flows and may relay media, inspect packets, or support firewall traversal.

Session Establishment Data (SED) is the information an outgoing SBE needs to route a call to a domain's ingress point. It may include a destination SIP URI, server name, port, transport protocol, and security parameters. The memo also distinguishes a service provider that supplies IP transport from a SIP service provider that supplies SIP session services.
sections.plainLanguage: An SBE handles call-signaling messages, while a DBE handles associated media. SED contains the information needed to route a session to the next provider's SIP entry point.

sections.title: Forms and Functions of Peering
sections.content:
Layer 3 peering connects IP networks to exchange IP packets and often uses BGP. Layer 5 peering connects SIP service providers to route call signaling; the associated media does not have to follow the same IP path.

Direct peering has no intervening session-layer network; indirect peering uses one or more transit networks. On-demand peering exchanges SIP traffic without prior association, while static peering requires prior agreement and configuration. The RFC names signaling, media, look-up, and location-routing functions.
sections.plainLanguage: Layer 3 peering exchanges IP traffic; layer 5 peering routes SIP session requests. Peering can use a direct connection or transit, and it can require prior setup or operate on demand.

sections.title: Federations and Common Rules
sections.content:
A federation is a group of SIP service providers that agree to exchange calls under shared administrative and technical rules. Rules may specify domain naming, codecs, authentication, transport protocols, or number-resolution methods.

A provider may belong to no federation, one federation, or several. It may also maintain bilateral peering relationships alongside federation membership. The RFC introduces federation as one example of static peering.
sections.plainLanguage: A federation is a group of providers that agree on rules for exchanging SIP calls. A provider can also have separate bilateral agreements or join more than one federation.
